name: Brain Before Sleep
look: A four-panel comic in a 2x2 grid in soft pink and gray tones. A pink cartoon brain with eyes speaks in a blank speech bubble, and a dark-haired woman in bed answers sleepily. Below, the brain speaks again, wide-eyed, and the woman lies wide awake staring into the dark.
use: Your brain keeps you up at night. It asks if you are going to sleep, you answer sleepily, then it brings up an embarrassing memory, a random worry or a pointless question, and you are suddenly wide awake.
slots: the brain's opening question (top left bubble)
the brain's intrusive thought (bottom left bubble)
examples: Remember when you waved back at someone who was waving at the person behind you?
What if we never locked the front door?
describe: brain asking if you are going to sleep then bringing up something embarrassing
cartoon brain keeping a girl awake at night
girl in bed with her brain talking to her
four panel comic of a pink brain and a woman who cant sleep
sleepy girl suddenly wide awake because of her thoughts
origin: A comic by Hannah Hillam for BuzzFeed, signed along the edge of the first panel.
